does_not_cover: Never computes a z or t interval from actual sample data end to end.
Never covers bootstrap intervals, bias, or sampling-design issues.
No hypothesis test is performed: no p-value, no power, no duality discussion.
notes: Non-technical by design; defers pdf and degrees-of-freedom theory. Warns against the n>30 z-substitution habit. Clear prerequisite: z-intervals with known sigma.

segments.topic: Scope: non-technical intro, math details deferred
Problem: sigma unknown, so s replaces it and Z becomes t
Shape: heavy tails, df grows toward the standard normal
95% z-interval recap with 1.96 and tail areas
t critical values by df from the table, e.g. 2.571 vs 2.042
Rule: always use t with sample s, regardless of size

suggested_locator: 00:18-01:58 for why t replaces Z; 05:50-07:46 for the critical-value table

teaches.why: Selects t critical values by df and mandates t over z with estimated spread.
Rebuilds the 95% z-interval with tail areas as the contrast case.
Explains s varies sample to sample, adding variability beyond sigma.
